Native production timers use paused Tokio time for deterministic 40 ms and 20 ms budget boundaries; Node callbacks use their original real synthetic timers. No wall-clock timing or local-model performance equivalence is claimed.
Full native request values are compared, including URL/method/headers and parsed request JSON; raw original request strings remain in capture. JSON key order is not a wire-byte equivalence claim.

The first cancellation regressions use positive pending-body observation and manually poll immediately after cancel. They do not satisfy body-release predicates by draining work after a returned error.

Awaited last-live cancellation waits only for the retained evaluator worker request/body lifetime; a live peer keeps shared work. Dropping the caller future is nonblocking cancellation, not an asynchronous join. Transport background ownership remains separate.

Final binaries compile only the clean 0e3ea4c base plus seven owned files with 379 unchanged scoped inputs. Concurrent SessionLog, StatusStore and Hyper/runtime ticket changes are not qualified by this isolated result.
